text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- In their fight to attract new customers Danish pension funds and life insurance companies are promising higher interest to savings account customers than profits permit.
--- Danish Liberal Party European politician Bertel Haarder is expected to become new vice-president of the European parliament in Strasbourg.

--- Danish companies are far more optimistic about turnover and profit prospects for 1997 than European colleagues, according to a survey of 5,000 companies in the European Union, Norway, Malta, Turkey and Switzerland.

--- Danish software producer Damgaard Data expects an international breakthrough after IBM's decision to globally market its Concorde economy system, allocating 100 million crowns to the project for both this year and 1997.
--- Thousands of new jobs have been created in Denmark's telecommunications and ancillary industries due to the recent liberalisation of the sector.

--- Not one single crown should be given away in pay rises at this spring's collective wage negotiations, Confederation of Danish Industries director Hans Skov Christensen says, basing his opinion on low German inflation and costs growth.
